current.title: Access-code batch generator + printable QR sheet in admin
acceptanceCriteria: A 'Print QR sheet' button appears on the Access Codes page (apps/admin) near the existing create/bulk controls.
Clicking it opens a print-optimized view rendering the currently-filtered codes (respect the active all/unused/used/revoked filter) as a QR grid.
Each cell shows a scannable QR encoding the access code string, the code text below it, and the label/game if present.
A print-only stylesheet hides the app chrome (nav/sidebar) so window.print() / browser print produces a clean sheet with multiple codes per page.
Both EN and HE strings are wired through the existing i18n dictionary (codes.* namespace) with RTL-safe logical classes.
implementationHints: Edit apps/admin/src/pages/AccessCodesPage.tsx; add new i18n keys to apps/admin/src/i18n/index.tsx under the codes.* namespace.
Add a small QR dependency to apps/admin (e.g. 'qrcode' to render to data URLs, or 'qrcode.react' component) — pure JS, no native deps; render code string as the QR payload.
Use a print-only CSS approach (@media print) or a dedicated printable container; can reuse APP_ID + existing CodeRow rows already loaded via onSnapshot — no new callables needed.
Keep neon/glass theme tokens for screen view but ensure print view is high-contrast (dark text on white) so QR codes scan.
Do not modify mobile scanning — encoding the code string is sufficient; scanning wiring is out of scope.
current.rationale: AccessCodesPage already has the full batch generator (create-one, bulk-create, live table, revoke/delete), so the only genuinely-new, high-value slice of T-0013 is the printable QR sheet. Organizers need a physical hand-out of codes on event day; a print-optimized QR grid turns the existing code list into something they can actually print and distribute. This is the highest-ranked candidate and a safe, additive, single-cycle deliverable that does not change any existing flow.
current.whyBeatAlternatives: It is the top-scored candidate (54) and ships concrete event-day organizer value, while H-REG/H-OFFLINE/H-DASH are player-side reliability polish that is lower-impact this cycle; it also avoids re-doing the batch generator that already exists.
current.visibleValue: An organizer clicks 'Print QR sheet' on the Access Codes page and gets a clean, print-ready grid of QR codes (each encoding its access code, with the code text + optional label/game beneath) that prints one-per-cell across pages.
current.downgradedFrom: T-0013 (full batch generator + QR sheet) — batch generator already shipped in AccessCodesPage; scope narrowed to the missing printable QR sheet slice

done.title: Control-room "needs attention" dashboard: one prioritized live view of active SOS alerts, teams past their station time cap, paused/closed stations, and pending judge reviews
done.notes: VERIFIED ABSENT on topographic-maps (no control-room/triage page exists). New admin page + nav entry for the manager role. Read-ONLY aggregation of EXISTING live sources (adminAlerts snapshot, listPendingArrivals, listTeams, task status + maxDurationMinutes) — add NO new gameState/score writes, reuse the existing acknowledge action. Bilingual EN/HE + RTL logical classes + the premium theme.
acceptanceCriteria: A new admin route (e.g. /control) is reachable from the top nav and gated to the manager/admin role via roles.tsx canAccess
The page shows distinct prioritized sections: Active SOS alerts, Teams over their station time cap, Paused/closed stations, and Pending judge reviews count
Each row deep-links or routes to the relevant existing page (Manager for SOS/stations, Judge/Check-ins for reviews) so the organizer can act
The view auto-refreshes (usePoll, ~10-15s) and renders clean empty states ('All clear') when a section has nothing
Sections collapse/hide gracefully and the whole screen has loading + error states; existing pages are unchanged
All new copy is bilingual EN/HE via the admin i18n dictionary and uses logical RTL classes
implementationHints: Add apps/admin/src/pages/ControlRoomPage.tsx; register the route in apps/admin/src/App.tsx and add a NAV_ITEMS entry + i18n key
Gate access in apps/admin/src/roles.tsx (ROLE_ROUTES) for manager/admin; consider making it the manager default home
Reuse callable<>() from services/api.ts and usePoll from hooks/usePoll.ts; do NOT hand-roll httpsCallable

SOS alerts + station status come from the same sources ManagerPage already reads; time-cap logic mirrors JudgePage's Task.maxDurationMinutes warning; pending reviews from listPendingArrivals / StationReviewPage
Import shared callable-result types from @rushpoint/shared (TeamSummary, PendingArrival, StationTeamRow) — don't redeclare
Add EN/HE strings to apps/admin/src/i18n and keep tokens/glass theme consistent with other pages
done.rationale: On event day the organizer has no single place to see what is going wrong right now — they must hop between the Manager, Check-ins, Station and Matchmaking pages to notice an active SOS, a team stuck past its station cap, a paused/closed station, or a backlog of pending judge reviews. A prioritized live 'needs attention' view turns scattered polling into one glanceable triage screen, directly improving organizer control and event-day reliability. It composes data from callables that already exist, so risk is bounded and it preserves all current pages.
done.whyBeatAlternatives: It is the highest-scored candidate (57) and uniquely improves real-time organizer control on event day, whereas H-REG/H-OFFLINE/H-DASH each polish one player edge case; the control room reduces the chance the whole event goes sideways unnoticed.
done.visibleValue: An organizer opens one screen and immediately sees, ranked by urgency, every active SOS alert, every team past its station time cap, every paused/closed station, and the count of pending judge reviews — with deep links to act on each.
